$comment: ARK-RAPID (ark-ydl) release manifest. Newest release first. Embedded in the assembly and served by /api/releases. 'current' must equal <Version> in Ark.Ydl.csproj (ReleaseTests checks it). compatibility levels: compatible | config | breaking. migration steps describe upgrading TO that release from the one before it; /api/releases/migration?from=x chains every step after x.

releases.title: Release tracking, audit log and admin console
releases.summary: The app now knows and shows its own release, records every request and download in a local SQLite audit log, and has an admin console with ready-made reports.

added: Version chip in the footer and an About dialog: this app's version, the version in its web manifest, the latest release and whether an update is available, with what changed and how to upgrade from any earlier version.

Audit log in {DataRoot}/audit/ark-ydl-audit.db (SQLite, written through Ark.Rapid.Database): every HTTP request, and every download with its link, title, channel, YouTube category (genre), tags, duration, format, size, outcome, IP, country/region/city, device, browser, OS, language and time zone.
Per-day rollups that outlive the raw rows, plus a retention period for the raw rows (Ydl:Audit:RetentionDays, default 365).
IP geolocation from the free DB-IP lite database, downloaded monthly into {DataRoot}/geoip (CC BY 4.0, attribution shown in the admin console).

Admin console at /admin: KPI tiles, daily trends, genres, top videos and channels, formats, countries, devices, an hour-by-weekday heat map, failure reasons, searchable download and request logs with CSV export, release and audit-store status.
POST /api/probe also returns categories, genre, channelId and language.
changed: GET /api/system gains 'release' and 'audit' objects. Nothing was removed or renamed.
The page sends an X-Ark-Client header (time zone, screen size, installed-app flag, page version) with its API calls.
yt-dlp download runs also append each item's metadata to a file in the job folder (--print-to-file), so playlist items get their genre too. Ydl:Audit:CaptureItemMetadata=false turns this off.
The service worker's cache is named after the release, so every release re-caches the page once.
security: The admin console needs an admin key (Ydl:Admin:Key, at least 16 characters) or, with Ark sign-in on, the Ark claim ark-ydl.admin. With neither configured it stays locked; auditing still runs.

api.notes: Additive only: new endpoints and new fields. Existing requests and responses are unchanged.

config.notes: New optional sections Ydl:Audit, Ydl:Admin, Ydl:Release and ArkDatabase. Every default works; the admin console only needs Ydl:Admin:Key or the Ark claim.

data.notes: Adds an SQLite database under {DataRoot}/audit and a GeoIP file under {DataRoot}/geoip. Nothing existing is touched. Rolling back to 1.0.0 simply ignores both.

deployment.notes: The publish output now carries SQLite's native library. A win-x64 publish needs a 64-bit app pool (Enable 32-Bit Applications = False); publish win-x86 for a 32-bit pool. If the library can't load, downloads keep working and the admin console reports the audit store as unavailable.

clients.notes: Open pages keep working. An installed app picks up the new page the next time it starts; its downloads list carries over.

migration.title: Unlock the admin console
migration.detail: Set Ydl:Admin:Key to a random secret of 16+ characters in appsettings.Production.json (or the Ydl__Admin__Key environment variable), then open /admin. With Ark sign-in on, granting the Ark claim ark-ydl.admin works instead.

migration.title: Keep {DataRoot} out of deployment deletes
migration.detail: The audit database lives in {DataRoot}/audit. The IIS layout in key_points.txt keeps data in C:\ark-ydl\data, outside the site, and is already safe. If DataRoot is the default App_Data inside the site, exclude App_Data from 'remove additional files' (Web Deploy) or mirror copies (robocopy /XD App_Data).

migration.title: Check the app pool's bitness
migration.detail: A win-x64 publish needs a 64-bit app pool. On a 32-bit pool, publish with -r win-x86 instead, or the audit store can't open (downloads still work).

migration.title: Allow the GeoIP download, or turn it off
migration.detail: Outbound HTTPS to download.db-ip.com fetches the monthly IP-to-city file (about 60 MB, once a month). Behind a strict firewall, upload an .mmdb and set Ydl:Audit:GeoIp:DatabasePath, use Ydl:Audit:GeoIp:Edition=country (4 MB), or set Ydl:Audit:GeoIp:Enabled=false.

migration.title: Decide how IPs are stored and for how long
migration.detail: Ydl:Audit:IpMode is Full by default; Masked drops the last octet (IPv4) or the last 80 bits (IPv6), Hashed keeps only a salted hash. Ydl:Audit:RetentionDays (default 365) prunes raw rows; daily totals stay. The page now tells users that requests are logged.

migration.title: Behind a proxy, trust forwarded headers
migration.detail: Behind ARR, Cloudflare or Application Gateway the audit log would otherwise record the proxy's IP. See key_points.txt step 7 (ASPNETCORE_FORWARDEDHEADERS_ENABLED). Ydl:Audit:CountryHeader (e.g. CF-IPCountry) takes the country from a trusted CDN header instead of GeoIP.

migration.title: Nothing to do
migration.detail: Reload an open page to see the version chip. An installed app updates itself the next time it starts.

releases.title: ARK-RAPID: the yt-dlp generation
releases.summary: A from-scratch replacement for the 2017 and 2020 downloaders: ASP.NET Core on .NET 10 driving a self-updating yt-dlp, so YouTube changes no longer break it. Every build deployed up to 2026-11-09 reported 1.0.0, including the later self-bootstrapping of ffmpeg and deno and the ARK-RAPID branding.

added: Extraction by yt-dlp: downloaded and SHA-256 verified when missing, self-updated every 24 h.

Video (144p to 8K, H.264/VP9/AV1, MP4/MKV/WebM), audio only (MP3, M4A, Opus, FLAC, WAV, OGG), clips with the most-replayed heat map, chapters, playlists and channels as ZIP, subtitles, thumbnails and SponsorBlock.
Downloads panel with live progress over Server-Sent Events, cancel, retry, preview and auto-save.
Installable app with an Android share target, a bookmarklet and swap-the-domain links (/watch?v=..., /shorts/..., /@handle).
ffmpeg and deno downloaded into {DataRoot}/tools when the server has none, so it runs on shared hosting where nothing can be installed.
Optional sign-in against the Ark identity server.
IIS (in-process) and container (Azure App Service) deployments.
security: Strict Content-Security-Policy, per-client rate limits and job limits, allow-listed sites with an SSRF guard, and argument lists (never a shell) for every tool.

api.notes: New HTTP API (/api/probe, /api/jobs, ...). Nothing from the legacy apps' MVC or Web API routes exists.

data.notes: The legacy apps stored nothing, so there is nothing to carry over.

deployment.notes: Needs the ASP.NET Core 10 Hosting Bundle and an app pool with No Managed Code, instead of .NET Framework 4.6.

clients.notes: Old bookmarks to the legacy pages do not resolve; YouTube links pasted or swapped into the new host do.

migration.title: Deploy ark-ydl as a new site
migration.detail: Follow key_points.txt (IIS) or the README (container). It is a new application, not an in-place upgrade.

migration.title: Revoke the legacy Google credentials
migration.detail: Immanuel.Yt.Cmments.Feedback/Key_points.txt holds a Google OAuth client secret and a YouTube Data API key committed to a public repository. Revoke or rotate both in Google Cloud Console; ark-ydl needs no Google key.

migration.title: Redirect and retire the old site
migration.detail: Point the old host name at the new site (or add a redirect), then remove the old site and its .NET Framework app pool.

migration.title: Use the new address
migration.detail: Paste any YouTube link, or replace youtube.com with the new host in the address bar.

legacy.name: Immanuel.Yt.Cmments.Feedback (2020)
legacy.stack: ASP.NET MVC 5 on .NET Framework 4.6, VideoLibrary 1.3.5 and the YouTube Data API
legacy.summary: Extracted stream URLs in-process with VideoLibrary; stopped working as YouTube changed its player, signature cipher and bot checks.

legacy.name: Immanuel.Yl (2017)
legacy.stack: ASP.NET MVC 5 on .NET Framework 4.6 with an in-repo copy of YoutubeExtractor 0.10.11
legacy.summary: Extracted stream URLs in-process with YoutubeExtractor; broken by the same YouTube changes.
